end.summary:
Discussed uses of oxygen, graphite, nitrogen, and carbon.
Explained oxygen in breathing and hospital oxygen cylinders.
Explained graphite’s soft layers and use in pencils.
Discussed nitrogen in fertilisers and plant protein; this was clarified during the lesson.
Carbon uses and rocket-fuel gases remained partly mixed up; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised linking each non-metal to a use, especially oxygen for breathing, graphite in pencils, and nitrogen in fertilisers. They explained graphite using its soft, sliding layers, and the nitrogen–protein connection was clarified later in the lesson. Carbon uses and the role of gases in rockets remained mixed up. At home, ask Pari to make a four-row table: non-metal, property, use, and one example.
